title: Nova Slate — feature scout and rough PRD
content:
Context:
Quick brain-dump about a small UX/config surface I keep imagining for enabling fast tradeoffs between latency/cost/quality for developers. Working title: 'Nova Slate' (slate = a compact preset for inference serving behavior). Aim is a lightweight, composable preset users can pick or author when wiring an endpoint in Console or via SDK params.

Why this feels useful:
- Many customers are iterating on cost/latency tradeoffs; current flow is too manual (model -> quant -> batch config -> caching) and hard to capture as repeatable templates.
- For demos/POCs we want one-click reproducible configs that encode sensible defaults for different goals ("cheap", "snappy", "high-fidelity", "session-optimized").
- Opportunity to surface operational signals (estimated tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens, expected p95) so devs can pick intentionally.

Core idea (sketch):
- Nova Slate = name + 3 required knobs + optional advanced toggles + preview estimate
  - Required knobs (user-facing): intent template (goal), model family variant, fidelity tier
  - Advanced toggles (hidden by default): quantization profile, KV caching policy, aggressive batching threshold, fallback variant
  - Preview: a readout using offline telemetry to show expected median latency, cost delta vs baseline, and compatibility notes (private deployment allowed?).
- Slate library: users can fork built-in slates, save to project or org-level, share slug with colleagues.
- SDK mapping: map slate -> query params for server (example: slate=snappy-v1 -> model=mistral-7b-opt, q=4-bit, cache=prefix, batch_hint=10)

User stories (rough):
- As an engineer building a chat assistant, I want a "snappy" slate so my dev environment mimics production latency targets without fiddling with batching or quantization manually.
- As a platform engineer, I want org-level slates so we can standardize cost targets across teams.
- As a solutions engineer, I want to create a "demo-high-fidelity" slate that locks model + slo so demos don't regress during sales cycles.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Console: create / select / save a Nova Slate on the endpoint creation flow (name, intent, model variant, fidelity tier).
- SDK: accept slate param in the request builder that maps to backend config (backwards-compatible fallback to explicit config).
- Preview widget: show quick estimated latency and estimated relative cost (using recent telemetry, ballpark numbers).
- Persistence: saved slates appear under project and can be toggled org-visible.
- Audit: saving a slate emits an audit log entry with owner and fields.

Telemetry & metrics to capture:
- Adoption: # of slates created per org, selection frequency per route, switch count between slates during an experiment.
- Economic impact: delta in tokens/second and cost per request when slate used vs baseline over a week.
- Safety signals: if a slate increases error rate or model falls back often, flag for review.

Rollout plan (low-friction):
1) Internal alpha: SDK + Console dropdown, no sharing, only project-visible. Limited to small pilot orgs.
2) Beta: add org-level sharing, preview estimates, and telemetry dashboards. Expose canary for 10% of traffic on selected orgs to validate economic predictions.
3) GA: public slates + template gallery + export/import.

Technical notes and mapping:
- Backend representation: compact JSON map: {"slate_id": "s-xxx", "model_hint": "mistral-7b", "quant": "q4_0", "cache": "prefix-v1", "batch_hint": 8, "fallback": "smaller-llm"} (this is internal, not final).
- Need a translator service that converts slate -> runtime config. Should be idempotent and versioned (slate versioning).
- Telemetry calc: use recent 7d/28d p50/p95 latency per model variant + historical token cost to compute preview. Fall back to conservative estimates if telemetry sparse.
- Security: org-level slates should be RBAC controlled; editable by org admins.

Design/UI roughs (notes to self):
- Minimal dropdown on endpoint builder: [Select Slate] -> inline preview card (p50, cost delta %, why pick this).
- "Edit advanced" expands to show toggles; hide quantization jargon under tooltips.
- Save dialog: Name + visibility + optional description + tags.

Open questions / decisions:
- Should slates be allowed to pin a specific model version (yes?) or only model family? Pinning helps reproducibility but causes more surface for drift.
- How to present cost estimate in a way that won’t mislead (range vs single number)? Probably a range with worst-case flag.
- Migration: if we introduce slate param vs explicit config, how to prioritize when both provided? Slate should be a higher-level override unless explicit configs present.
- Billing: tie cost estimates to real billing only after GA; previews should be labeled "estimate".

Experiment ideas (quick):
- Pilot with two customers: one AI-native startup (wants perf) and one enterprise (wants reproducibility). Track time-to-first-successful-deploy and post-deploy regressions.
- A/B test: default to "balanced" slate vs no-slate baseline and measure retention of demo flows for trial users.

To-do (short):
- Wire a quick prototype in Console (dropdown + preview stub). (me)
- Draft SDK param mapping PR and compatibility tests. (Devon)
- Telemetry query: small job to compute weekly p50/p95 per model/variant. (Rowan)
- Sync with legal on audit retention for org slates.

Notes to self (choppy):
- Keep scope tiny for alpha: name + 3 knobs + preview + persistence. Avoid share gallery initially.
- Could be a way to productize Redwood's own best-practices (ship built-in slates like "redwood-snappy-v1").
- This might pair well with Optimize recommendations: auto-propose a slate after analyzing a workload.

End of jam notes. Will clean into PRD skeleton if this feels promising after pilot chat with Rowan/Devon.
